source: CPTS Module 03: Network Enumeration with Nmap

examples.label: Full port range with service versions

notes: Press Space during a scan for a live status line; -v/-vv increase verbosity. -A is shorthand for -sV -O --traceroute -sC combined. For OS detection alone: -O --osscan-guess. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 6 (Information Gathering).

references.title: HTB Academy - Network Enumeration with Nmap

recommended.note: Default+vuln scripts on the open ports.
Pivot to FTP enumeration if 21 open.

name: Nmap - Full Port Version Scan
description: Scan all 65535 ports with version detection - the thorough service inventory of a host. Add progress and tracing for long-running scans.

variations.label: OS detection with aggressive guess (OSCP Ch6 canonical)
variations.command:
sudo nmap -O <ip> --osscan-guess
# -O = enable OS detection (requires root)
# --osscan-guess = lower the confidence threshold; still reports best guess even when match is ambiguous
# Follow with -sT -A for service+script details on the same host

defense.why_it_works: A full version scan (-sV, typically with -p- across all 65535 ports) probes every open port to fingerprint each service and version — comprehensive but slow and highly visible.
defense.impact: A complete service-and-version inventory of the host.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046 AN1583] Monitor for execution of network enumeration utilities (nmap, netcat, net.exe, ping.exe, tracert.exe) in short succession, particularly when chained with lateral movement tools or system enumeration commands. [AN1584] Sequential ping, arp, or traceroute commands issued from bash scripts or interactive shells to map remote hosts are a strong behavioral indicator.
defense.artifacts: Sustained probing across all ports — a large, easily detected footprint in IDS/firewall logs.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1046 M1042] Disable or remove unnecessary services and functionality that expose attack surface. [M1030] Implement network segmentation to limit the set of hosts reachable from any given compromised system. Use firewalls to restrict which source addresses can reach each service port.
defense.evasion: Run a quick port-only scan first (-sS -p-) to identify open ports with minimal traffic. Then run version detection (-sV) targeted only at discovered open ports. This approach causes significantly less traffic than a combined full-port version scan and reduces the risk of being discovered and blocked by security mechanisms.
defense.misconfiguration: Network perimeters that do not filter ICMP, do not use egress filtering, or expose unnecessary services (all ports open) allow comprehensive port scanning. Systems without host-based firewalls or IDS/IPS allow scan traffic to enumerate every open service, revealing attack surface. No rate-limiting on inbound probes means stealth scans complete quickly.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No firewall between attacker and target (or overly permissive rules):
# iptables -L  ->  Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)  [no rules]
# Or: Windows Firewall disabled
# Every service's port is reachable from any source

# No IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata not deployed; no AWS GuardDuty / Azure Defender
# Nmap SYN scan completes in seconds with no alert generated
defense.secure_config:
# Linux host-based firewall — default-deny inbound:
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
# Only open required services:
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # HTTPS only
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 10.10.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT  # SSH from mgmt network

# Rate-limit scan detection (drops SYN floods):
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s --limit-burst 3 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -j DROP

# Deploy IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata rules detect nmap OS detection probes
# AWS: GuardDuty (detects port scans from EC2)
# Cloud: Security Groups default-deny with explicit allow rules
